subject: Private deployment: steps for customer-controlled storage & deletion ops
messages:
From: Sara Parker <sara.parker@novamed.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: novamed-security@novamed.com
Date: 2026-10-20 09:12 PDT
Subject: Private deployment residency + deletion process (info request)

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we evaluate Redwood Private for NovaMed's patient-facing workloads, our security and compliance team needs a concise operational description that explains:

- Where customer data lives (control plane vs data plane) when Private is deployed into our VPC
- How long snapshots / backups may persist and how retention is controlled
- Exact steps we (the customer) will run to execute a tenant deletion and how we can verify zero copies remain
- KMS/HSM integration options for customer-managed keys and how key destruction impacts retained data

Can you share a short ops flow and a tentative SLA for deletion timelines on contract termination? If you already have a one-page attestation or checklist we can attach to our SOC review, that would be ideal.

We are aiming to finalize vendor selection by mid-November.

Thanks,
Sara Parker
Director, IT Operations
NovaMed Health
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Parker <sara.parker@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20 11:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Private deployment residency + deletion process (info request)

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Happy to provide an ops-level flow and an engineering-runbook. I pulled in Aditya from our Infra team to give the technical steps and timelines.

High level answer (summary while Aditya writes up the playbook):
- Data plane lives in the customer's VPC/subnet(s) — we only manage a minimal control plane for orchestration.
- Persistent storage is mounted into the customer's project; snapshots are tenant-scoped and deleted per configured retention; we support shortest retention windows under Private (customer-controlled).
- Deletion is a two-step process: (1) customer triggers tenant destroy (we provide a CLI/API in your VPC) which removes live volumes and KV cache; (2) background verification job confirms absence of mounted volumes and rotates audit state — we provide checksums and logs for your audit.
- KMS: we support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via customer KMS; if you destroy the key, any encrypted backups are irrecoverable.

Next steps: Aditya will attach a concise playbook and a sample SLA window (48–72 hours typical for complete removal in our standard Private offering; we can discuss contract language for a faster committed window). Also attaching a short walkthrough link and will follow with attachments.

Would you like a 30-minute ops walkthrough this week or next?

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Parker <sara.parker@novamed.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21 10:22 PDT
Subject: Re: Private deployment residency + deletion process (info request)

Sara — following up with the technical playbook and concrete verification steps. Attaching two docs: vpc-deletion-playbook.pdf and kms-integration-guide.pdf (see attachments). Also uploaded a short slide deck to the Drive link Tessa shared.

Technical summary (actionable):
1) Data residency model
   - Control plane: Lightweight service managed by Redwood in our control network (no tenant data persisted).
   - Data plane: All persistent volumes (object/block) are provisioned in the customer's VPC and account; storage endpoints are under your network ACLs. Metadata that must be surfaced to the control plane is minimised and hashed; no PHI/PII is sent to Redwood-managed services unless explicitly enabled.

2) Retention and snapshots
   - Snapshots are tenant-scoped. Retention policy is configured per-tenant via the Private config (default 30 days). You can set retention to 0 for immediate deletion of snapshots on destroy.
   - Snapshots are stored in customer-controlled buckets/accounts when configured; otherwise, they are kept in an encrypted project-controlled bucket that we can designate under your tenancy.

3) Deletion workflow (customer-initiated)
   - Step A: Customer runs `rictl tenant destroy --tenant-id <TID> --force` in their bastion (we provide the client binary and auth hooks). This unmounts volumes and sends a destroy request to the data-plane agents.
   - Step B: Data-plane agents remove live volumes, drain caches, and issue asynchronous snapshot deletion jobs. Jobs are logged to the tenant audit stream with a unique job id (JOB-xxxxx).
   - Step C: Background verification (48–72 hours by default): periodic scanner validates no mounted volumes, no active snapshots, and no KV entries. Scanner produces a signed report (SHA256) and stores it in the tenant audit location.
   - Step D: Final attestation: we provide a signed Delete Attestation PDF and an audit log bundle (log rotation retained for 90 days by default; retention can be contracted).

4) KMS and key lifecycle
   - BYOK: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) via a key ARN/policy. Encrypted artifacts are encrypted under your key.
   - Key destruction: If you schedule key destruction, encrypted snapshots/archives become cryptographically unrecoverable; we flag remaining artifacts in the audit bundle and include key destruction timestamps.

5) Verification artifacts we provide
   - Signed delete attestation (PDF)
   - Job IDs and signed checksum report for removed volumes
   - Audit log bundle and storage bucket link

SLA guidance (example contract language):
- Standard: Full deletion attestation within 72 hours of successful destroy job completion.
- Contracted: We can commit to 24 hours for an additional enterprise SLA fee and operational runbook (please escalate if needed).

Operational exceptions / edge cases:
- If cross-region replication was enabled, deletion must be run in each replica region (we provide cross-region job orchestration).
- If you enabled third-party backup exports (to a vendor-managed bucket), you must revoke access or delete those exports separately; we will enumerate any known external exports in the attestation.

I attached the playbook (vpc-deletion-playbook.pdf) and the KMS integration guide. Let me know your tenant IDs and whether you prefer encrypted snapshots to live in your own storage account. Happy to run a dry-run with your security team.

— Aditya Rao
SRE Manager, Infra — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-21 15:40 PDT
Subject: Re: Private deployment residency + deletion process (info request)

Thanks Aditya — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifications before scheduling the walkthrough:

- Can you confirm the default retention configuration is tenant-level and not overridden by any control-plane-wide policy? We want a contractual guarantee that retention is per-tenant.
- For the signed attestation: will the attestation include a list of buckets/ARNs where artifacts lived so we can validate removal on our side?
- Our compliance team would like the option to purchase the 24-hour deletion SLA for critical tenants. Can you share pricing or internal steps to enable that in our contract?

If you can send the one-page attestation template, we will attach it to our vendor review. Also, we are fine with a short ops dry-run next week (Thu or Fri morning PT).

— Sara
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Parker <sara.parker@novamed.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-22 16:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Private deployment residency + deletion process (info request)

Sara — great questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Retention scope: confirmed — retention is tenant-scoped and configurable per-tenant. We'll include a clause in the vendor addendum that retention settings cannot be overridden without the tenant owner's explicit approval.
- Attestation contents: yes — the Delete Attestation includes job IDs, timestamps, and the list of storage locations (bucket ARNs / volume ids) at the time of deletion.
- 24-hour SLA: we can offer the contracted 24-hour deletion SLA as an add-on. I'll loop in our Pricing & Contracts team for numbers and will send a scoped amendment draft for review.

I'll schedule a 30-minute ops dry-run for Thu 2026-10-29 09:00 PT (proposed). Please confirm and share the Tenant ID(s) you want us to use for the dry-run.

Attachments: residency-walkthrough-slides.pptx (link in body), vpc-deletion-playbook.pdf, kms-integration-guide.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the run-through.

— Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
